sources.title: Revised Statutes of Anguilla, Chapter P120, Public Entertainments Tax Act
sources.said: "entertainment" includes— (a) any cinematograph entertainment; (b) any theatrical performance, variety entertainment or conjuror's entertainment; ... 2. There shall be charged, levied and paid in respect of every payment for admission to any entertainment a tax (hereinafter referred to as "entertainment tax") at the rate of 10% of the amount of such payment exclusive of the entertainment tax ... 7. (1) The Governor in Council may, upon it being proved to his satisfaction— (a) that the net proceeds of any entertainment are not intended to be for private gain or profit but are to be devoted wholly to philanthropic, charitable, religious or educational purposes ...; (b) that the entertainment is of a wholly educational character; or (c) that the entertainment is intended for the amusement of children; remit the entertainment tax or any part thereof

found.notes: No theatre tax incentive: the only tax law naming theatre charges 10% on admissions, remittable for non-profit, educational or children's shows.
